purpose: Private editorial intake from the Daily Intelligence Briefing. This file is never published directly.

entries.title: AI detection velocity can exceed human remediation capacity
entries.summary: Continuous AI-enabled security testing can improve discovery while creating a remediation backlog faster than the organisation can safely validate, prioritise and close it.
entries.whyItMatters: A faster detector is not automatically a stronger control environment when validation, change authority and remediation throughput do not scale with it.
entries.controlImplication: Measure discovery-to-remediation capacity and make queue re-sequencing authority explicit before expanding autonomous scanning or patching.

entries.title: An agent’s authority envelope now spans applications, identities and transactions
entries.summary: As agents move from a single application into browsers, productivity suites and external services, the relevant control surface becomes the authority the agent can exercise across that environment.
entries.whyItMatters: The traditional unit of application risk is too narrow when one delegated identity can discover, select and act across multiple systems.
entries.controlImplication: Map delegated identity, persistent credentials, action limits and revocation across the full workflow rather than assessing an agent as a standalone application.

entries.title: Human approval only works when it is bound to the action that executes
entries.summary: A human can approve one operation while mutable workflow state causes a materially different operation to execute later. The control objective is approval-to-execution integrity, not simply a human-in-the-loop checkpoint.
entries.whyItMatters: Process maps can show a human approval while the technical system no longer guarantees that the approved context, parameters and action remain the same.
entries.controlImplication: Require deterministic or tamper-evident binding between the exact action reviewed, its parameters and its execution record for consequential agent workflows.

entries.title: Agent action completeness is becoming a control objective
entries.summary: When external agent activity is discovered late or by outside researchers, the question is no longer only whether the agent crossed a boundary. It is whether the firm can reconstruct every credential use, data transfer and attempted boundary crossing.
entries.whyItMatters: Partial telemetry weakens containment, incident response, disclosure and assurance at exactly the point autonomous activity needs stronger evidence.
entries.controlImplication: Define an action-completeness standard for material agents: attributable identity, immutable event capture, complete external-action telemetry and independent evidence of containment.
